## For Marta

**What changed:** When someone asks "which bikes are free from this date to that date?", the answer now comes back more than 200 times faster. The list of bikes you get is the same as before, in the same order (cheapest first).

**Why it matters:** With 400 bikes and 50,000 bookings, the old search took about 225 thousandths of a second (0.225 s) every time. Now it takes about 1 thousandth of a second (0.001 s). Staff and customers no longer wait on the search, and it can handle many searches at once without slowing down. It also leaves room for the shop to keep growing its booking history.

**What did not change:** Which bikes show as available. A bike with a booking that overlaps the dates is still hidden. A bike whose previous booking ends the same day the new one starts is still offered.

## How much faster (measured)

I timed the search on made-up data of the same size as the shop: 400 bikes, 50,000 bookings, and a 3-day search window. Each result is the average of 20 searches.

| | Time per search |
|---|---|
| Before | 225 ms |
| After | 0.7 to 1.0 ms (three runs) |

That is roughly 225 to 320 times faster.

## What I checked

- The two existing tests pass.
- I compared old and new code on 200 random small cases. Both returned identical lists in identical order.
- The before and after runs on the large data returned the same 371 available bikes.

## What I did not check

- Real shop data. The timings use generated bookings, so your real numbers will differ somewhat.
- The full website or app. I timed only the search step, not page loading or the network, so the wait a person sees will improve by less than the search step alone.
- Timings come from one computer, so treat them as approximate.

## Technical summary

`findAvailable` in `src/availability.js` checked every bike against every booking (about 400 × 50,000 comparisons). It now makes one pass over the bookings, records the IDs of bikes with an overlapping booking in a `Set`, and then filters the bikes by that set. Cost drops from O(bikes × bookings) to O(bikes + bookings). The overlap rule and the sort order (price, then id) are unchanged.
